title: Easy-to-Use Phones for Seniors: Simple Phones, Plans and Smartphone Shortcuts
subtitle: Big-button phones, senior-friendly plans and free settings that make a regular smartphone simpler.
excerpt: You do not need a complicated phone to stay in touch. Here is how simple flip phones, senior plans and the free simple modes on iPhone and Samsung compare, with real prices.
author: Nickel And Gadget Editors

sections.content: Modern phones can do almost anything, and that is exactly the trouble for many of us. Tiny icons, pop-up updates and menus that change every few months can turn a simple call to a grandchild into a small ordeal.

The good news is that you have real choices. You can buy a phone built to be simple from the start, or you can take a regular smartphone and strip it down to the few things you actually use. Here is how each path works and what it costs.
Two ways to get a simpler phone
Buy a phone made to be simple

Senior-focused phones put big buttons, loud speakers and short menus first. Some are flip phones with real keys you can feel. Others are smartphones with a plain list menu instead of screens full of apps. Most are sold with their own service plans, so budget for the monthly bill, not just the phone.

Lively, the company behind the Jitterbug phones, sells its phones only with Lively service. Its flip phone plans run from $14.99 to $44.99 a month, and smartphone plans from $19.99 to $49.99, plus taxes and fees, according to Lively's plan page. Those prices assume a $5 paperless billing discount, and Lively lists a $35 one-time activation fee and a $3.23 monthly admin fee.

In June 2026, Consumer Cellular launched SpeakEasy, a separate brand it says is created specifically for adults age 75 and older. Its plans start at $14.95 a month for the flip phone and $19.95 for its smartphone, with unlimited talk and text, according to the company's announcement.
Simplify the phone you already have

If you or a family member already owns an iPhone, Apple's Assistive Access trims it down to large, easy buttons for a handful of apps such as Calls, Messages, Camera and Photos. Apple suggests a trusted supporter, like an adult child, help set it up. You start in Settings, then Accessibility, then Assistive Access.

During setup you choose the apps, pick a Rows or Grid layout, and create a separate Assistive Access passcode. That passcode is needed to leave the simple mode, so write it down somewhere safe. Apple notes that if it is forgotten and no recovery account was set up, the phone may need to be reset.

Many Samsung Galaxy phones have a similar feature called Easy mode. According to How-To Geek, you open Settings, tap Display, then Easy mode, and switch it on. Icons, text and the keyboard get bigger, and a longer touch-and-hold delay helps prevent accidental taps. Not every Android phone has it, so check your model.
What to look for before you buy

items: Add up the real monthly cost: plan price, admin fees, taxes and any extra service such as emergency response.
Ask whether the phone is locked to one carrier. Jitterbug phones work only with Lively, while the RAZ Memory Cell Phone is unlocked.
If you wear hearing aids, look for a hearing aid compatibility rating on the product page.
Check whether an emergency or help button works on the plan you choose. On Jitterbug phones, Lively's Urgent Response service requires a Preferred or Premium plan.
Ask about free trial months or return windows, and keep the receipt and box.
Bring a family member to help move contacts and photos from your old phone.

sections.label: Good to Know
sections.content: A help button is not the same as calling 911. On Jitterbug phones, the dedicated button connects to Lively's Urgent Response agents only if you pay for that service. In a true emergency, dialing 911 directly is always an option on any working phone.

There is no single right answer. If you want buttons you can feel and a phone that mostly makes calls, a flip phone with a senior-friendly plan is simple and affordable. If you already own a smartphone, try Assistive Access or Easy mode first; it costs nothing. And for a loved one with memory loss, a caregiver-managed phone like the RAZ may bring the most peace of mind.

products.name: Jitterbug Flip3
products.price: About $79.99 for the phone (list price; $59.99 on sale, October 2026), plus a Lively plan from $14.99 a month, a $35 activation fee and a $3.23 monthly admin fee
products.blurb: A flip phone with big, backlit buttons, a loud speaker and voice dialing, plus a Help button that connects to Urgent Response if you add that service. Rated HAC 2019 for hearing aid compatibility.

products.name: Jitterbug Smart5
products.price: About $119.99 for the phone (list price; $89.99 on sale, October 2026), plus a Lively plan from $19.99 a month
products.blurb: A smartphone with a 6.75-inch screen, large text and a simple list-based menu, for people who want photos and video but fewer choices. It has a dedicated Urgent Response button for the optional 24/7 service.

products.name: RAZ 64GB Memory Cell Phone
products.price: About $369 for the phone (list price at Lively, October 2026), plus a separate service plan; check current plan prices
products.blurb: Built for people with memory loss or dementia: the user taps and holds a contact's picture to call, and a caregiver manages contacts and settings from the free RAZ Care app. Apps and web browsing are not available.
